payload.feature:
A brief README, measured by one goal. The operator ruled in chat on 2026-09-02: the goal is to optimize time to first visible customer-perceived value. The README is the first thing a stranger reads, so every line on the front page earns its place by shortening the path from landing on it to seeing Brokkr prove something: a run lit with one command, and its journal, graph and the reviewer's verdict on screen. Measure the page against that path: install, one command, proof on screen, then the map for whoever wants to dig deeper or extend. Anything that does not shorten that path moves to the docs.

The current README is far too much (1,022 lines, fourteen sections); it becomes a brief front page with a map of the docs and links for whoever wants to dig deeper or extend, and nothing that belongs in a guide stays on the front page.

Enact:

1. README.md becomes a front page under 150 lines: the name and the one-line positioning (coordination tools help agents work together; Brokkr proves what they did), what it is in one paragraph, install in one command per channel exactly as the release and packaging paths already publish them, a sixty-second quickstart of one run, then a map: where to read next (guides, the decision record, the essays, the lore, the evidence shelf, contributing, architecture), one line each with a link and the sharpest sentence about it. Then the acknowledgment (SwarmForge, decision 0019 ruling 7, unchanged in substance) and the licence line. No section may be a summary of a guide that exists; it points at the guide.

2. Nothing is lost. Every section leaving the README moves whole to a home under docs/: the read surfaces, recipes and composition, the agent library, provider adapters, secrets, the journal and verification, the repo layout, the decision culture, and the essay list, either into the existing guide that owns the subject (docs/guides/quickstart.md, recipe-authoring.md, driver-authoring.md, versioning.md, docs/essays/README.md, docs/decisions/README.md) or into a new docs/guides/<subject>.md when none owns it; docs/guides/README.md (new, or docs/README.md) is the index the front page's map points at. Move text as text: no rewriting beyond the sentence that stitches it in.

3. Tests and workflows that read README.md keep passing by moving what they pin or updating them, whichever is honest: crates/brokkr-cli/tests/packaging.rs, crates/brokkr-cli/tests/rename_guard.rs, crates/brokkr-cli/tests/init_stacks.rs, crates/brokkr-cli/src/init.rs, crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs and its agent tests, crates/brokkr-core/tests/differential.rs, .github/workflows/ci.yml and release.yml. The rename residual guard still scans the new front page and every new guide.

4. The contributing fire running beside this one (contributing-goes-through-brokkr-0fbcddeb) rewrites CONTRIBUTING.md and the README's contributing section; this fire keeps the README's contributing entry to one line pointing at CONTRIBUTING.md, so the two land without a fight.

Verification: cargo fmt --check, clippy, the full test suite, and the exact coverage gate at 100% lines, branches and functions. Windows CI: any path inside an sh -c script uses forward slashes and quotes, and every read is read -r.
